supportingSources.label: PAPA Mata Hari tutorial with Bowen Kerins
Trent Augenstein at Fairfax Pinball Open 2014

strategy.summary: Test the top saucer, collect it four times for 5x Bonus X only when its kickout is safe, then build base bonus through repeatable A-B orbits.

steps.text: Try to plunge the ball into the top-center saucer. Watch the kickout before you depend on this shot.
If the kickout is safe, lob the ball into the saucer four times.
modeNotes: Top saucer: Each collect scores 3,000 and advances base bonus three times.
Second collect: Lights 2x and the left outlane for 50,000.
Third collect: Lights 3x and the right outlane for 50,000.

steps.text: If a kickout heads down the middle, use a small cabinet movement while the ball is in the saucer. Stop if the tilt margin is small.
After 5x is lit, use the A-B lanes and orbits to build base bonus. Each A or B scores and advances base bonus by 1,000.
Shoot the A-B lanes, orbits, inlanes, and safely presented drop targets until base bonus reaches 29,000. At 5x, the end-of-ball bonus is 145,000.
Use the long bottom-to-top orbit when it can collect one letter and feed the ball through the other letter.
Do not force the drop bank. Finish it only when six or seven targets are already down, or after base bonus is full.
Protect the end-of-ball bonus. If the ball enters a lit outlane, accept the 50,000 rather than risk a tilt.

quickInfo.name: Top saucer
quickInfo.summary: Four collects advance Bonus X to 5x; the second and third also light the left and right outlanes for 50,000.

quickInfo.name: A-B
quickInfo.summary: Completing A and B advances its award from 1,000 through 5,000, then Extra Ball and Special.

quickInfo.name: Drop bank
quickInfo.summary: Completing all eight drops scores 50,000; the second completion also qualifies the target Special award.

quickInfo.name: Base bonus
quickInfo.summary: Targets and lanes build base bonus to 29,000, collected at the end of the ball with the current Bonus X.

fallback.title: A-B orbit loop
fallback.when: Use this plan when the top-saucer kickout is unsafe.

steps.text: Shoot the safer A-B orbit from the bottom toward the top.
Try to let one orbit collect both A and B.
Each A-B completion raises its award from 1,000 through 5,000.
A sixth completion lights extra ball. Later completions can light special.
If the event converts extra ball or special to points, keep repeating A-B.

alternatives.title: Finish the drop bank
alternatives.when: Use this plan when six or seven drops are down, or when base bonus is full.

steps.text: Finish all eight drop targets for 50,000.
Finish all eight a second time for 50,000 and special.
Stop if the horizontal rebounds are not controlled.
Collect the top saucer four times for 5x Bonus X.
Shoot the A-B lanes, orbits, inlanes, and safely presented drop targets until base bonus reaches 29,000.

techniques.name: Saucer lob
techniques.instruction: Use a soft, rising shot that drops into the top saucer. A direct shot can hit the lip and reject.

techniques.name: Saucer-kickout adjustment
techniques.instruction: If the kickout heads down the middle, use a small cabinet movement while the ball is in the saucer. Do not move the cabinet when the feed is already safe.

techniques.name: Dead bounce
techniques.instruction: Dead bounce a clean saucer feed to the opposite flipper when that route reaches a safer cradle.

techniques.name: Bottom-up A-B orbit
techniques.instruction: Shoot an A-B orbit from the bottom toward the top. A full orbit can return through the other letter and collect both.

techniques.name: Side-post nudge
techniques.instruction: Use a small nudge when the ball reaches a side-lane rubber post. Try to move the ball toward an inlane.

cautions.issue: The top-saucer kickout can feed straight down the middle.
cautions.response: Test it on the plunge. Use a small movement while the ball is in the saucer, or use the A-B fallback.

cautions.issue: A direct top-saucer shot can hit the lip and reject.
cautions.response: Use a soft lob that drops into the saucer.

cautions.issue: An A-B orbit return can skim a sling or reach an outlane.
cautions.response: Test each orbit. Repeat only the direction with a controlled return.

cautions.issue: Drop-target hits create horizontal, uncontrolled rebounds.
cautions.response: Wait until six or seven targets are down, or until base bonus is full.

cautions.issue: A save attempt at a lit outlane can tilt away its 50,000 award and the built bonus.
cautions.response: Accept the drain when 50,000 plus the built bonus reaches the target score.

checkBeforePlay: Confirm the stock 1978 Bally rules; aftermarket code can change Bonus X, saucer, A-B, and scoring behavior.
Confirm Extra Ball and Special conversion, ball count, Bonus X, A-B, drop-bank, outlane, tilt, and tournament settings.
Test the saucer entry and kickout, both A-B orbits, eight drops, bumper exits, slingshots, side posts, outlanes, and tilt margin.

noteDetails.label: Top-player proof
items: At the Fairfax Pinball Open 2014, Trent Augenstein and Brian Shepherd used the top saucer to reach 5x, then repeated A-B to fill the 29,000 base bonus.

strategy.simpleOverview: Mata Hari uses four top-saucer collects to reach 5x Bonus, then builds base bonus through the A-B orbits. Repeat the saucer only when its kickout is safe, raise the base to 29,000, and protect the 145,000 end-of-ball collect.
strategy.overview: In Mata Hari, four top-saucer collects raise Bonus X to 5x, while each A or B lane adds 1,000 to base bonus. Test the saucer kickout before repeating it, then loop A-B toward the 29,000 base maximum. Finish the drop bank only when nearly complete and avoid tilting away the multiplied bonus.
